title: Deep Questions to Ask Your Partner to Deepen Your Connection
summary: These are the deep questions to ask your partner that helped me build real intimacy. Use them to spark honest, meaningful conversations and feel closer.
body_markdown:
## 10 Deep Questions to Ask Your Partner


#### Intimate Questions to Ask Your Partner About Emotional Connection


1. **Have I been behaving in any ways lately that make me seem more distant or unavailable?**
It’s not always easy to receive, but asking your partner if you’ve been unintentionally pushing them away can help support understanding and connection. Sometimes we can put up walls or mentally check out without even realizing it.
2. **Do you feel that we’re as emotionally connected as you’d like us to be?**
This is a good question to leave open-ended and allow your partner space to answer honestly. Give them the floor and be sure to share your own response to the question, too.
3. **What are some things I do that make you feel the most appreciated?**
Deeper conversations with a partner don’t always have to feel heavy or foreboding. You can – and should – ask some positive and heartfelt questions to get a sense of what is going well in your relationship.
4. **What is something specific that made you fall in love with me?**
Even if you’re going through a rough patch, reminiscing with your significant other about the early stages of falling in love can really help spark that intimacy and affection again. It’s also a good way to balance some of the tough truths that can come up when you’re both working through more intense feelings together.
5. **Is there anything that you have not been able to get off of your mind lately?**
The answer to this question may be totally unrelated to you or your relationship, but it’s a nice way to show your partner that you really care about how they’re feeling. Not only as your loved one, but as a person. If they’re feeling anxious about work or stressed by family or finances, they’ll be glad you’re open to being a listening ear and that they can lean on you.
6. **How do you prefer that I communicate when I’m having an intense feeling about something you said or did?**
Some couples prefer to communicate important feelings in the moment, while others are more avoidant and tend to let things stew before any confrontation happens. It’s healthy and normal to fall somewhere in the middle, so this question can help you both figure out the best ways to prevent reactionary behavior but still address issues before they become overwhelming.
7. **How do you think we have been handling conflict recently?**
Whether you’re in a newer or more long-term relationship, it’s normal to avoid conflict, sometimes for the sake of keeping the peace – even our own peace. Conflict resolution is an important skill to learn as a romantic partner. Be honest with yourself about where you think you stand in that sense, and be open to hearing their perspective, too.
8. **What would you do or say if you thought you were having doubts about our future?**
Although it may feel scary, it’s not a bad idea to bring up these kinds of topics when you’re progressing into more serious stages of a relationship. Moving in together, getting engaged, planning a family – each of these are big steps that should involve a lot of communication and honesty.
9. **How would your friends or family react if you told them we were separating?**
We all say things we don’t mean sometimes, and everyone needs space to vent or seek outside advice when it comes to their romantic relationships. But if your partner seems hesitant to answer this question or appears to be answering dishonestly, you may want to consider how they are representing you to the other people in their life.
10. **What values do you think we share, and where do we differ?**
If you view your significant other as your life partner, sharing at least some of the same core values is important. If you want to start a family together or if you end up going through a tragedy, illness, or other difficult situation with them, you’ll want to know that you’re both on the same page about what you find most important in life.
